_comment: Golden set v2 floors (the Phase 14.0 plan, section 14.0 / P14-D4). Recorded by block 14-A2 (T14.0.5). T14.2.8 (block 14-C2) turns enforcement on PER METRIC (the `enforce` object below) instead of 14-A2's single global `enforce_now` switch: a metric is enforced once its floor is both in force (14.2 onward, i.e. every floor here) and actually met by the measured numbers; `enforce_now` is kept only as a human-readable note of when enforcement as a concept started, no longer read by gate.py.
_enforce_comment: block 14-C2 (T14.2.8): noisy_recall (1.000), greeting_reply_p95_s (~1.48s) and router_p95_s (~1.05s local) enforced from that block. Block 14-C3 (T14.2.9, DEC-062) adds follow_up_resolution: measured 0.900 on BOTH final verification runs (gate-20261125T130554Z-2888977.log and gate-20261125T131222Z-2925883.log, --only eval, n=10 follow-up turns after this block's +4 dialogues) -- clears the 0.85 floor reliably, not a one-off, so enforced from this block on. 14-C3 also left intent_accuracy at 0.840 (below its 0.90 floor, DOWN from 14-C2's 0.873 on the smaller 63-turn fixture) -- a router ambiguous-vs-followup boundary confusion on terse, several-turns-back follow-ups (DEC-063). Block 14-C4 (T14.2.9-fix, DEC-063 = B) fixes it: one more contrasting few-shot plus a deterministic, code-level tie-breaker (`router._resolves_a_reference`) that corrects an 'ambiguous' verdict to 'followup' whenever conversation context existed AND the model's own standalone_query already resolved the reference from it (live-verified against the real router on both DA-14-C3 regression cases before the gate runs below). Measured 0.907 on BOTH final `--only eval` runs (gate-20261125T180052Z-3120649.log and gate-20261125T180723Z-3121974.log, n=75) -- clears the 0.90 floor reliably on both, so `intent_accuracy` is enforced from this block on. `conversational_reply_rate` also measured 1.000 on both of the SAME two runs (up from 14-C3's 0.944) but is left `false` here: DEC-063/this block's scope was intent_accuracy + follow_up_resolution only, and two runs on one fixture is a thinner basis for a metric this block did not set out to fix -- left for whichever block next touches conversational replies (T14.3/14-D1) to decide, not assumed here. Flipping intent_accuracy to `true` without first raising the real number would fail `gate.sh --full` outright; the two runs above prove the floor is genuinely met, not a one-off.
